page: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.12xlarge is an extreme memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The server is powered by 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC 9R05 x86_64 processor clocked at up to 5.0 GHz, configured with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio without simultaneous multithreading. It provides an expansive 1536.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, establishing an allocation of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector extensions, bfloat16, and VNNI instruction sets alongside AES and SHA cryptography extensions. Local high-performance storage is directly integrated via a 3800 GB NVMe SSD, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps.

Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional performance across compute, memory, and transactional throughput categories. The system achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core CPU testing, recording a Geekbench 6 single-core score of 3104.0 and multi-core score of 32628.0, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 116535.23. The memory subsystem delivers uncached read bandwidth of 533.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 213.84 GB/sec, driving massive in-memory throughput evidenced by 176.8 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and top-tier PassMark database operations scores. Although lacking hardware GPU acceleration, the 48 dedicated cores and extensive memory bandwidth sustain efficient LLM inference for small and medium model prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x8aedz.12xlarge delivers high resource density for workloads that would otherwise require multiple smaller instances or sprawling distributed clusters. Bundling high-capacity NVMe storage and massive DDR5 memory directly with dedicated high-frequency compute cores minimizes serialization and network latency overhead. Primary tradeoffs include the lack of GPU hardware for matrix-heavy training tasks and zero bundled public IPv4 addresses. The instance is optimal for large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA or Redis, real-time analytics engines, distributed memory-bound ETL workflows, and heavy database virtualization.
